task: nl-gap remote source of e-w-melee: forge.trigger.combat.melee_hit observed on the host from the replicated melee damage

patchTarget.rva: 0x138076D (the body's own entry; ForgeEnemy's evidence/e10-damage-window.json records the same member)
patchTarget.patchForm: [HarmonyPatch(typeof(Dam_EnemyDamageBase), "ReceiveMeleeDamage")] — the member is `protected`, so the patch names it as a string; ForgeMap's player-side hook patches the same member name on Dam_PlayerDamageBase the same way
patchTarget.forgeEnemyOverlap: ForgeEnemy patches Dam_EnemyDamageBase.ProcessReceivedDamage (the shared accept path its own damage facts read) and does NOT patch ReceiveMeleeDamage, so this row's hook is the only patch on this member — checked before the hook was written, as ruling 103 requires

fields.source: Agents.pAgent (+0x8) — a packed replicator handle with `bool TryGet(out Agent)` (Agents.pAgent, dumpLine 680479)
fields.damage: UFloat16 (+0xA) — packed, and its decode scale belongs to the receiver's own body, so this half never decodes it
fields.staggerMulti/precisionMulti/backstabberM: UFloat16 — multipliers, not this row's ports

packet.missing: the packet carries no charge state, so the row's `charged` port stays absent on this source

ports.source: the packet's pAgent resolved through TryGet(out Agent) and TryCast<PlayerAgent>(), then the same player-reference lookup the other sources use (EquipmentNativeAdapter.OwnerOf)
ports.target: the receiver's own Owner (EnemyAgent) resolved through the kernel's enemy kind
ports.damage: the receiver's Health before and after the body ran: the damage that really landed. A hit the receiver's rules reduced to nothing, a rejected hit and a kill all read as the health difference the body produced, and a difference of zero or less publishes nothing
ports.charged: absent — the packet has no charge state

dedupe.rule: MeleeHitLedger.PublishesRemote(attackerIsLocal, attackerIsBot) is false for this machine's own player and for a bot, because those swings are published by the hit entry that performed them (MeleeWeaponFirstPerson.DoAttackDamage / MeleeWeaponThirdPerson.DoAttackDamage); the receive half publishes only a remote player's swing
dedupe.whyTheyOverlap: the machine that swings sends the damage to itself as well (Dam_EnemyDamageBase.MeleeDamage goes through SendPacket + SendLocally, per ForgeEnemy/VALIDATION.md), so on the host a local swing reaches both this receiver and the first-person hit entry
dedupe.secondHalf: MeleeHitLedger.TryClaim(source, target, limb, tick, world) is checked and claimed by both halves, so one landed hit is published once even if a packet is delivered twice; a claim is live for MeleeHitLedger.WindowTicks (8) ticks and never outlives its world epoch
dedupe.test: ForgeWeapon/tests/WeaponFacts/MeleeDedupeTests.cs (6 cases) drives the ledger and the ownership rule without a game

hooks.prefix: reads the receiver's Health before the body runs and the packet's source and limb; a receiver whose health cannot be read is not remembered, so the postfix has nothing to pair
hooks.postfix: reads Health again, computes the landed damage, resolves the attacker and the enemy life and publishes through WeaponMeleeHitFacts.RemoteHit
hooks.reentrancy: one pending slot keyed by the receiver's pointer; a postfix whose receiver does not match the pending prefix publishes nothing
hooks.guards: both halves run inside WeaponNativeSession.Guard, so a hook that fires with no session, on the wrong thread or after a fault does nothing; every native read is inside its own try/catch and no exception can leave a patch

cases: one hit is claimed once inside the window
a different limb, target or attacker is a different hit
a claim never outlives its world
a hit without a nameable attacker or target is never claimed
the receive half publishes only a remote player's swing
the ledger keeps a bounded number of claims
testCoverage.note: the hook bodies themselves are only compiled by the native build (the mirror project); the focused cases cover the rule the two sources share
